texts.facts: Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of t he PFA Act and Rules. As per the complaint, on 16.06.2005 the Food Inspector(herein after referred as FI) Dr. Pramod Kothekar purchased a sample of 'Paneer" a food article for analysis from accused C.V. Singh at M/s Flavourz Family Restaurant, Shop No.4, Dayanand Vihar, Vikas Marg, Delhi - 110092, where the said food article was found stored for sale and where accused C.V. Singh was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling. The sample consisted 750 gms of Paneer taken from an open freezer bearing no label declaration. The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh. S.P. Bhardwaj, SDM/LHA. The sample was taken after cutting the Da vs C.V. Singh on 3 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33121095/ 1 Paneer into smallest possible pieces with the help of a clean and dry knife in a clean and dry tray and mixed properly with the same knife in same tray. The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts by putting them in three separate clean and dry bottles. 20 drops of formalin was added in each sample bottle. Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles. Notice was given to accused C.V. Singh and the price of sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 16.06.2005. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by F.I. were signed by accused C.V. Singh and the other witness Sh Jagdish Prasad, FA, Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came (award, as such Sh Jagdish Prasad, FA was joined as witness. DA vs C.V. Singh 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. 23/LHA/11695 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same to be adulterated. The report of the Public Analyst is as follows: "The sample does not conform to the standard because milk fat of dried matter is less than the prescribed minimum limit of 50%" 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused C.V. Singh was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Flavourz Family Restaurant, Shop No.4, Dayanand Vihar, Vikas Marg, Delhi - 110092 at the time of sampling and as such he was incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop. 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 31.01.2006 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a)&(m) of PFA Act, 1954 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused. 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 31.01.2006. The accused thereafter exercised their option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act. Based on the report of the CFL as well as evidence led in pre charge evidence, charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being DA vs C.V. Singh violation of Section 2(ia)(a)&(m) of PFA Act, to which accused person pleaded not guilty and claimed trial . 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined four witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 SDM/LHA Sh S.P. Bhardwaj, PW-2 FI Dr. Parmod Kothekar, PW-3 FI Ranjeet Singh and PW-4(inadvertently mentioned as PW-3) FA Sh Jagdish Prasad. PW-2 FI Dr. Parmod Kothekar and PW-4 FA Sh Jagdish Prasad were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh S.P. Bhardwaj. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the Da vs C.V. Singh on 3 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33121095/ 2 sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample commodity of "Paneer" 750 gms from the vendor for analysis, bearing no label or declaration, taking the sample of Paneer after cutting into smallest possible pieces with the help of a clean & dry knife in a clean and dry tray, dividing the sample into three equal parts by putting them into three separate clean and dry sample bottles, putting 20 drops of formalin in each sample bottle, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice in form VI Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C. The accused furnished statement Ex.PW1/D. The raid report Ex.PW1/E was prepared at the spot. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample along with one copy of memo in form VII and another copy of memo in form VII in sealed deposited with PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/G on 17.06.2005. The remaining two counter parts of the sample in intact condition along with two copies of DA vs C.V. Singh memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited on 17.06.2005 with LHA vide LHA Receipt Ex. PW1/F, under intimation that one counterpart of the same has already been deposited with PA. Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW1/H was received, according to which the sample was not conforming to the standards because milk fat of dried matter is less than the prescribed minimum limit of 50%. Thereafter PW-1 further investigated the matter and sent letter Ex.PW2/A to STO Ward No. 83 and received its reply. After completion of investigation, the entire case file was put before then Director PFA Shri Diwan Chand for obtaining his Consent. The then Director PFA granted his Consent for prosecution vide sanction order Ex.PW2/C. Thereafter, the present complaint Ex. PW2/D was filed before the Court. Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/J alongwith copy of PA Reports was sent to the accused vide postal receipt Ex.PW1/K. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel. 8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 31.05.2016 wherein the accused persons denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter matter was listed for defence evidence. 9. In his defence, the accused examined Sh Ramesh Kumar and Sh Manoj Chand Joshi as DW-1 & DW-2. The accused also examined himself as DW-3. Thereafter defence evidence was closed vide order dated 22.05.2017 and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: It is submitted that the paneer of which the sample was taken was meant for preparation of "paneer tikka". The accused has relied upon the judgements titled as Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs Laxmi Narayan Tendon etc. 1975(II)FAC 444; AIR 1976 SC 621 and followed in M.N. Chaudhary vs State of Bihar & Ors 2007(I)FC 106, K.P. Tensing & Anr vs D. Jayachandran 2011 (I)FAC 328, C.S. Ram Mohan & Ors vs State of AP & Ors 2007(I)FAC1990 and Roopak Kumar vs State of Bihar 2014(I)FAC 198. In all these cases it was held that the raw materials collected from the vendors, which was to be used as an ingredient for preparation of the food, cannot be said to be a food article for sale under the PFA Act. In K.P. Tensing & Anr vs D. Jayachandran 2011 (I)FAC 328 while referring to Laxmi Naryana DA vs C.V. Singh Tendon's case(supra), the Hon'ble Kerala High Court observed :- "In view of the decision of the Apex Court, it can only be found that Food Inspector is not competent to take sample of wheat powder, which was kept at the hospital canteen for purpose of preparation of food and not kept or stored for sale. In such circumstances, based on the report of examination of such sample, first respondent is not competent to lodge a complaint for an offence under the Act, as has been done by Annexure-A complaint" 14. Similarly, the Hon'ble Jharkhand High Court in M.N. Chaudhary's case (supra) observed that "In L.M. Batra vs State of Bihar 1995(I) 209, Patna High Court held that if an article of food is not stored in the sense that it was stored for sale, Food Inspector could not be acting within his powers to enter and inspect that place and take sample of that article. Unless that article is stored for same, the Food Inspector will not be competent under the law to take a sample or on such sample being found adulterated validly managed prosecution therein. The sample of sale collected from the store of Hotel, Ranchi Ashok did not amount to be kept for sale and therefore, the prosecution is not maintainable against the petitioner Managing Director. In the present case also the mandatory provision of Section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954 as well as Rule 9(B) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rule, 1955 have not been complied, which authorized a legal right to the accused to get the sample re-analyzed by the Central Laboratory on the receipt of the report by the petitioner within 10 days of the report of the Analyst and therefore, the Court finds DA vs C.V. Singh that the petitioner has been deprived of the valuable right conferred under Section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rule 9(B) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rule, 1955". 15. One more point raised is that the sample was not representative because of variations in PA report and CFL report. The argument of the Ld. Defence Counsel on the basis of which acquittal is sought at the threshold in this matter is thus, 'since there is variation of more than 0.3% in the reports of PA and CFL, the samples were not representative'. Pointing out the above said variation in the two reports it is contended that the same would be sufficient to conclude that samples were not taken by the FI in proper manner and were not representative, for which benefit should be given to the accused. 16.In this regard, the defence strongly relies upon the judgement titled as Kanshi Nath v. State [2005(2) FAC 219], informing that the said ruling has been followed by the Hon'ble High Court of Da vs C.V. Vinod Kumar Gupta [2010(2) JCC 957], State v. Virender Kohli [2014(2) FAC 223], State v. Kamal Aggarwal [2014(2) FAC 183], State v. Vidya Gupta [2014(1) FAC 291], State v. Dinesh Goswami [2014(1) FAC 302], State v. Mahabir [2014(1) FAC 286], State v. Santosh Sharma [2014(1) FAC 296], Raja Ram Seth & Sons v. Delhi Administration [2012(2) FAC 523], State v. Sunil Dutt [2011(4) JCC 2377] and State v. Rama Rattan Malhotra [2012(2) FAC 398].
